Double burden of malnutrition

Source: R/ref-classify.R
wgh_dbm.Rd

Individual double burden is stunting together with overweight or obesity in the same child at the same visit. Population double burden is defined by the WHO thresholds: a group has a double burden when stunting (or thinness) prevalence is at least undernutrition_threshold and overweight or obesity prevalence is at least overweight_threshold.

Usage

wgh_dbm(
  x,
  by = "sex",
  undernutrition_threshold = 10,
  overweight_threshold = 20
)

Arguments

x

Classified data (see wgh_classify()).

by

Grouping columns for the population indicator.

undernutrition_threshold, overweight_threshold

Prevalence thresholds in percent (WHO: 10 and 20).

Value

A list with individual (data with column dbm_individual) and population (prevalences and a logical dbm_population by group).

Examples

cl <- wgh_classify(growdat)
wgh_dbm(cl, by = c("sex", "site"))$population
#> # A tibble: 6 × 8
#>   sex    site      n stunting thinness overweight_obesity dbm_individual
#>   <fct>  <fct> <int>    <dbl>    <dbl>              <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 Male   Site1  2869    1.36      4.25               34.7         0.488 
#> 2 Male   Site2  1237    0.566     4.77               39.3         0.0808
#> 3 Male   Site3   519    1.16      1.93               49.9         0.385 
#> 4 Female Site1  2568    0.896     3.74               19.2         0.156 
#> 5 Female Site2  1062    1.04      2.07               24.1         0     
#> 6 Female Site3   408    2.94      1.72               26.2         0.245 
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: dbm_population <lgl>
